section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Torah is analogous to a human being, composed of a body and soul, corresponding to the commandments and the Torah itself, and that Torah study relates primarily to the soul while fulfilling commandments relates to the body.
section.t: And it is written,
"This is the Torah, a man,"
that the Torah is in the likeness of a man.
For just as a man is composed of a body and a soul,
so too is it in the Torah, which has a body and a soul.
And in general, this is the distinction between Torah and commandments.
For the 248 positive commandments are the 248 limbs of the King,
analogous to the limbs of the body,
and the Torah is the blood, which is the soul,
that draws vitality into the limbs of the commandments.
And this is that the commandments are in time and place, while the Torah is above time and place
[therefore, anyone who engages in the study of the burnt-offering is as if he offered a burnt-offering,
even when it is not the time or place of the offering],
for the body, which is physical, is bounded by time and place,
while the soul, which is spiritual, is above time and place.
And just as it is in the Torah and commandments themselves,
so too is it regarding the connection of the Torah and commandments to the person who studies and fulfills the commandments.
For the study of Torah relates primarily to the soul, and the fulfillment of commandments to the body.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that although in revelation the Torah is higher than the commandments, in their root the commandments are superior, being G-d's will which is above His wisdom, and the Torah serves as an explanation of the commandments.
section.t: And it is known
that this—that the Torah is above the commandments—is as the Torah and commandments are drawn down in revelation,
but in their root,
the commandments are more elevated.
For the Torah is His wisdom, and the commandments are His will,
will which is above wisdom.
And moreover,
even after the Torah and commandments come into the chain of descent, the superiority of the commandments is evident,
for the Torah is the explanation and elucidation of the commandments.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that similarly, the root of the body is higher than the root of the soul, as G-d's love for Israel through their body stems from His essential free choice, which is above the natural love for their souls.
section.t: From this it is understood,
that so too is it with the soul and body in man
[which are analogous to Torah and commandments],
that although the vitality of the body comes from the soul,
the root of the body is higher than the root of the soul
[and as explained elsewhere,
that the love and connection of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel by virtue of their soul,
"You are children to the L-rd your G-d,"
is like a natural love, so to speak,
analogous to the love of a father for his son.
That is,
the root of this love is from a level where there is a place for the beloved,
and it is not from His very Essence.
However, the love and connection of the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel by virtue of their body,
is
(not due to the virtue of the body,
nor even the virtue of a son,
an intrinsic virtue,
but rather)
from the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose the body of Israel,
with free choice,
and this choice is from His very Essence].
And this itself—that the soul is drawn to enliven the body—is because of the superiority of the body by virtue of its root
(in analogy to this, that the Torah explains and elucidates the commandments,
because the commandments are higher than the Torah).
